# AGENTS.md

Every session reads this file first, in every harness. With `docs/agents/` it is the
canonical policy, and its rules bind every role.

## How to start

- Read this file, then your role's file: `docs/agents/planner.md`, `docs/agents/builder.md`
  or `docs/agents/reviewer.md`.
- habit starts every session and invokes every user-invoked skill. A start instruction names
  the role, the target and the skills, in the same words in every harness, for example
  `Role: Builder. Ticket: #<n>. Skills: tdd.` or, for a spec approved for whole-spec
  delivery, `Role: Builder. Spec: #<n>. Skills: implement-spec, tdd.` Asking habit to start
  a session takes a start request (Talking to habit and to other agents).
- A session holds one role. A subagent acts in its parent's role, which its task names.
- A session started without a role is read-only. habit's explicit request for a change makes
  it a Builder (`builder.md`, A direct request).
- Every session acts on GitHub as the agent account, the machine's own `gh` login.

Each harness takes the start instruction its own way:

- **Claude Code**: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` translates this file for it.
- **OpenCode**: `opencode --prompt "<start instruction>"`; a skill is `@name`. Waiting on a
  PR is unverified there, so stop and say what you wait for.
- **deepseekharness**: a desktop session's first message, or
  `dsh --profile headless "<start instruction>"`; a skill is `/name`. habit picks the sandbox
  mode, the generator never runs there, and waiting is unverified: stop and say. With no
  machine rules against `ghm` or Actions-secret writes, those limits rest on instructions.
- **Codex harness**: the first message of a Local-mode app chat in this repository's
  directory, never Worktree mode; a skill is `@name` in the app and `$name` in the CLI. habit
  picks the sandbox, and the generator never runs there. Keep this repository trusted and
  run no cloud tasks. Each poll waits at most 5 minutes.

## Flow at a glance

Orientation only; the role files and `review.md` hold the rules.

1. A Planner turns an idea, an incoming issue or a bug into tickets habit approves, and a
   dispatch plan.
2. habit starts a Builder on a ticket, or on a spec approved for whole-spec delivery.
3. The Builder implements, self-verifies and opens one PR declaring its risk tier; a
   results-comment ticket ends without one (`builder.md`).
4. The tier's reviews run (`review.md`, Minimum reviews).
5. habit reads the Merge summary and merges with the pinned merge command.

## Hard limits

- No agent merges, enables auto-merge, force-pushes, rewrites pushed history, or changes
  rulesets, repository or Actions settings, or Actions secrets.
- No agent calls habit's account alias, `ghm`, even to run a command a handoff gives habit.
  Machine rules deny it in Claude Code and OpenCode, and partly in the Codex harness.
- No agent discards work it doesn't own: another session's branch, worktree or uncommitted
  changes.
- **Planner**: writes the tracker freely, and the repository only for `GLOSSARY.md` and ADRs,
  through its own docs PR; never product code.
- **Builder**: one delivery, one ticket or one spec habit approved for whole-spec delivery,
  in a fresh session; one branch and one PR unless `builder.md`, Results-comment tickets,
  applies. It edits its ticket only after habit's agreement is
  recorded there.
- **Reviewer**: only at medium and high, in a context that didn't write the change. It never
  pushes, and never edits the PR, tickets or labels.

## Talking to habit and to other agents

- **Agent to agent**: on GitHub, in English. Nothing a later session needs lives only in a
  terminal.
- **Agent to habit**: in the terminal, in plain Chinese, with governance terms and product
  names in English and no code, diffs or paths. Each message names its sender and target.
  Requests and handoffs follow `docs/agents/handoff.md`, where only the Planner arranges
  what comes next.
- **A start request**, asking habit to start a session, has two marked parts. "给 habit" says
  where to open the session, which model, why, and any shared resource it takes. "粘贴给 agent" is one start
  instruction, never a list of options.
- **habit's decisions** made in the terminal that a later session needs are written back to
  GitHub.
- **Summaries**: the Merge summary and the high-risk report keep an English copy on the PR.
- **Voices**: the Builder doesn't speak for the Reviewer, and the Reviewer doesn't commit the
  Builder to changes.

## Governance files

- **Fixed content** is what a notice "Generated by governance model version N" covers: a
  whole file, the record's `confirmed` part aside, or the text between a file's governance
  markers; text after the end marker is repository-owned. Only the generator changes fixed
  content, and a needed change goes to habit as a governance model change.
- **The governance record**, `.github/governance/record.yml`, holds the sensitive paths, the
  required checks and the agent account. Its `confirmed` values change only in a delivery
  that quotes habit's request verbatim, never on an agent's own initiative, even to add
  protection.
- A change to the required checks needs habit's owner-script rerun after it merges.
- Committed governance wins over a skill's text that disagrees with it; report the conflict
  to habit.
- A relied-on skill missing from the machine stops the session; tell habit.
- The instruction files are this one and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, so every harness loads the
  same policy. A root `CLAUDE.md`, an `AGENTS.override.md` or a `.codex/` directory would
  split it, and the repository holds none.

## Secrets

- Never read, print, commit or post a credential. Name one only by its type and location,
  never its value, even to habit or in a miss record.
- Only habit writes Actions secrets, in the browser, from the settings link and exact name a
  session gives, never through a command run in a session. Machine rules back this in
  Claude Code and OpenCode, and partly in the Codex harness.
- Check the staged files before every commit, and never bypass push protection.
- **A blocked push**: rewrite only your own unpushed commits, or reshape a fake fixture;
  otherwise stop. Tell habit the type and location, and habit decides on rotation.
- **An exposed credential**, merged or not: tell habit at once, by type and location, and
  remove the value where you can, by a new commit, deleting your own comment or editing a
  body. habit rotates it, whoever's it is, and nobody rewrites history. Open a miss record
  (`issue-tracker.md`, Miss records) and hand habit a start request for its `retro`. A
  credential from before governance gets the same response but no miss record, and its
  removal is a ticket. A private repository follows the same steps.
- **Visibility** changes only by habit, through a session. Private to public: warn that the
  history and Actions logs become public, then hand habit the change and an owner-script
  rerun as one pair. Public to private: warn that GitHub's credential detection and blocking
  end there.

## Code Review Rules

These rules bind every review, each review bot's included. How they apply is in
`docs/agents/review.md`.

### Risk tiers

A change takes the highest tier any part of it reaches.

| Tier | The change |
| --- | --- |
| low | A two-way door with a small blast radius, touching no sensitive path, covered by its verification. Examples: docs, copy, comments, tests, internal refactors that keep behavior, small tested fixes, additive changes behind a default-off flag |
| medium | Ordinary product changes, such as user-visible behavior or an interface, CLI or API. Also dependency changes, build or CI configuration, shared modules, a medium-floor sensitive path, and a re-landed outside change |
| high | One-way doors: data migrations, destructive operations, releases and publishing. Also authentication, privacy and secret handling, an Actions secret's use added or changed included; production resources; a broad blast radius; a change that loosens governance or its enforcement; a high-floor sensitive path; and the generator's output |

- **Trusted authors** are habit and the agent account; anyone else's PR is an outside PR
  (`docs/agents/builder.md`, Outside PRs).
- **Sensitive paths** are listed once, with their floors, in
  `.github/governance/record.yml`: the defaults, each with a medium floor, and the
  repository's confirmed ones, medium or high. A change touching one, by a deletion or
  either side of a rename too, takes at least its floor.

### Findings

- **Important** blocks the merge while open:
  - a review bot's Important finding (`review.md`, Review bots);
  - a security review's HIGH or MEDIUM;
  - a declared tier below what the change warrants;
  - a review or authorization exception stated anywhere broader than at its narrowest
    (`review.md`, Exceptions);
  - a required check's rerun-only pass with no linked open issue for its cause (`review.md`);
  - an edit to fixed content in any PR but the generator's own: a file whose notice says
    only the generator changes it, the record's `confirmed` part aside, or the text between
    governance markers;
  - a credential value in a diff, PR text or comment, named by its type and location only.
- **Nit** never blocks: a review bot's Nit; a security review's LOW.
- **Pre-existing** never blocks: anything the change didn't introduce, whatever its
  severity.

### The tier challenge

Classify the tier from the change itself, by the risk tiers and the sensitive paths' floors,
and compare it with the PR body's `Risk: <tier> — <reason>` line. A declared tier below
yours is an Important finding that names the warranted tier and why. A review bot's tier
finding binds only as an Important finding.

### From round 2

A review covers only what changed since the last reviewed head, plus the open findings. It
posts nothing twice, and names each finding's bug class so the Builder fixes every
instance. Nits come in round 1 only, at most three.

## This repository

### Product and repository boundaries

- Squirrel is the macOS Swift/AppKit frontend for Rime. It receives librime's already-ranked
  candidate list and renders, paginates and highlights that order. Candidate generation,
  scoring and reranking belong outside `sources/`; reserved-property hints are cosmetic.
- The custom reranker and semantic-memory implementation live in
  `Habit130/librime-llm-rerank`, not here or in a submodule. Their issues, specifications,
  decisions and dependency edges stay in `Habit130/squirrel`; code PRs go to the plugin
  repository and follow its own instructions and tests.
- `origin` is `https://github.com/Habit130/squirrel`, the only write remote and PR target
  for this repository. `upstream` is `https://github.com/rime/squirrel`, a read-only
  reference. Do not routinely merge or rebase upstream into this intentionally divergent fork.
- The default branch is `master`; local `master` tracks `origin/master`, never upstream.
  Branch names use `<type>/<kebab-slug>`. Do not stack PRs.
- Before a GitHub write, `gh repo set-default --view` must report `Habit130/squirrel`.
  Stop if it names upstream. Explicit repository targeting still follows the tracker guide.

### Product review expectations

Apply the fixed Code Review Rules above, with these Squirrel-specific expectations:

- Preserve user text: commit exactly once through the text client, and leave neither marked
  text nor active composition stranded during deactivation or global cleanup. Preserve the
  documented unavailable-client fallback and key-event consumption semantics.
- Preserve canonical facts and atomic outcomes: a successful fact operation must not corrupt
  unrelated facts or expose a partial old/new state.
- Keep private input and credentials within their declared trust boundaries. Recording and
  experimental activation require the explicit opt-in specified by the product contract.
- Stale or incompatible versioned state is a documented failure or fallback, not a successful
  semantic result. Ranking failures preserve the supported original-order fallback.
- Keep ranking out of `sources/`. Findings identify the trigger, impact, primary evidence
  and safe path; these expectations do not narrow the fixed finding categories.

### Product context routing

| Work | Repository context |
| --- | --- |
| Swift/IMK lifecycle, keys, candidate UI, configuration, installer commands or manual validation | `.agents/skills/squirrel-input-method-architecture/SKILL.md` |
| Ranking, semantic memory or LM integration | `CONTEXT.md`, applicable `docs/adr/`, and `docs/reranker-public-contract.md` |
| Personal BGE experiment | `docs/personal-experiment-profile.md` in addition to the ranking context |
| Personal Qwen + LoRA live-reranking exception | `docs/adr/0005-personal-lora-live-reranking.md` in addition to the ranking context |
| `data/luna_pinyin.custom.yaml` | Its constraint header, before editing; this checked-in patch is the deployment truth source |

`CONTEXT.md` covers candidate ranking after candidate generation, not all of Squirrel. Use
its vocabulary within that scope; frontend lifecycle, marked text, panel geometry and
deployment use the architecture skill and surrounding code's vocabulary. A missing frontend
term in the ranking context is not a glossary gap. Work spanning both areas reads both.
Merging an experimental ADR or profile is not live enablement.

The ranking layers remain librime core for dictionary/user weights and candidate composition;
octagram for schema-enabled grammar reranking; Lua for schema-configured extensions; predict
for next-word prediction; and the custom plugin for this fork's reranking and semantic memory.
Octagram needs its binary, grammar data and schema enablement together; bundled recipes provide
zh-hant grammar data, not a zh-hans grammar package. Acquisition and build-path details are in
`docs/agents/build.md`.

### Machine-level shared resources

Before concurrent work, establish one exclusive owner for each applicable shared resource:

- **librime build tree** (`librime/build/`, `librime/plugins/`, `lib/`, `bin/`): one writer
  for plugin installation or engine builds. A binary-only consumer copies its inputs out first.
- **Live Rime deployment**: one owner for deployment or live-input verification. Evaluation
  and baseline work use a throwaway `rime_dir`, not the live user-data directory.
- **Quiet machine**: one owner when the deliverable includes latency or timing measurements.

Unresolved ownership blocks the affected concurrent work. Machine-specific instances are
located in the ignored `.local/agent-context.md`, never credentials. GitHub tickets and PRs
are the record. Once a closed ticket's result is on GitHub, its ignored local evidence,
worktrees and handoffs may be removed; whatever an open ticket, an open PR or a running
machine service still uses is kept and named in `.local/agent-context.md`.
